title: At the Train Station
subtitle: A tourist talks with a station attendant. Each scenario adds one new layer.

scenarios.japanese: 東京に行きたいんですけど。。。
scenarios.romaji: Tōkyō ni ikitai n desu kedo...
scenarios.english: So, I'd like to go to Tokyo...

scenario.setting: At the ticket counter — a tourist approaches the station attendant.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 東京に行きたいんですけど。。。
lines.romaji: Tōkyō ni ikitai n desu kedo...
lines.english: So, I'd like to go to Tokyo...

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: はい、わかりました。こちらへどうぞ。
lines.english: Yes, of course. Please come this way.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: まずはきっぷですよね。一人ですか？
lines.romaji: Mazu wa kippu desu yo ne. Hitori desu ka?
lines.english: First the ticket, right? Just one person?

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: はい、一人です。
lines.english: Yes, one person.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: かしこまりました。少々お待ちください。
lines.english: Certainly. One moment, please.

contextNotes: 〜たいんですけど。。。 softens a request by trailing off. The けど isn't "but" — it's a polite hedge that leaves room for the listener to help. This hanging sentence is very Japanese.
へ marks direction ("toward"). Compare it with に in later scenarios.
〜よね seeks agreement ("right?") — softer than a plain confirmation.
お〜ください is a polite request form. Recognize it here; you'll produce it much later.
かしこまりました is service keigo for "certainly."

quiz.prompt: Where is the tourist trying to go?
quiz.wrongAnswerExplanation: The tourist says 東京に行きたい — they want to go to Tokyo.

quiz.prompt: What is the attendant asking at the end of the dialogue?
quiz.wrongAnswerExplanation: The attendant was essentially asking if the tourist was traveling alone, or if they only needed 1 ticket.

scenarios.japanese: 東京までは、二千三百円です。
scenarios.romaji: Tōkyō made wa, nisen sanbyaku en desu.

scenario.setting: Still at the counter — the tourist asks the fare and pays.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: すみません、いくらですか。
lines.english: Excuse me, how much is it?

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: 東京までは、二千三百円です。
lines.romaji: Tōkyō made wa, nisen sanbyaku en desu.
lines.english: To Tokyo, it's 2,300 yen.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 二千三百円ですね。
lines.english: 2,300 yen, got it.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: お支払いは現金ですか、カードですか。
lines.romaji: Oshiharai wa genkin desu ka, kādo desu ka.
lines.english: Will you pay by cash or card?

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 現金でお願いします。
lines.english: Cash, please.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: ありがとうございます。少々お待ちください。
lines.english: Thank you. One moment, please.

vocabulary: お支払い / おしはらい
contextNotes: まで marks the endpoint ("as far as / to"). Listening focus: parsing にせんさんびゃくえん as one number.
Note さんびゃく (300) — the h→b sound change is a real beginner stumble.
〜ね confirms back what you heard — a genuine, usable comprehension-check move.
AですかBですか offers an A-or-B choice.
〜でお願いします means "[do it] with/by ___, please." Hugely reusable: 現金で, カードで, 急行で.

scenarios.japanese: あちらの階段を上って、右側です。
scenarios.romaji: Achira no kaidan o nobotte, migigawa desu.
scenarios.english: Go up those stairs, and it's on the right.

scenario.setting: Near the gates — the tourist asks which platform and how to get there.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 東京行きは、何番線ですか。
lines.english: Which platform is the Tokyo train?

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: 三番線です。
lines.english: Platform 3.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 三番線は、どこですか。
lines.english: Where is platform 3?

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: あちらの階段を上って、右側です。
lines.romaji: Achira no kaidan o nobotte, migigawa desu.
lines.english: Go up those stairs, and it's on the right.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 階段を上って、右ですね。
lines.romaji: Kaidan o nobotte, migi desu ne.
lines.english: Up the stairs, then right — got it.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: はい、そうです。
lines.english: Yes, that's right.

vocabulary: 何番線 / なんばんせん
contextNotes: 〜行き attaches to a destination to mean "bound for."
〜て、〜 chains two actions in sequence ("do X, then Y"). This first multi-step instruction is the difficulty bump.
The learner repeats the sequence back with ね, reinforcing the て-chain by re-saying it.
そうです confirms "that's right."

scenarios.japanese: 次の急行は、十時十五分です。
scenarios.romaji: Tsugi no kyūkō wa, jūji jūgofun desu.

scenario.setting: On the platform — the tourist checks the next train and picks one.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 次の電車は、何時ですか。
lines.romaji: Tsugi no densha wa, nanji desu ka.
lines.english: What time is the next train?

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: 次の急行は、十時十五分です。
lines.romaji: Tsugi no kyūkō wa, jūji jūgofun desu.
lines.english: The next express is at 10:15.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: 急行ですか。普通もありますか。
lines.romaji: Kyūkō desu ka. Futsū mo arimasu ka.
lines.english: The express? Is there a local too?

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: はい。普通は、十時半に出ます。
lines.romaji: Hai. Futsū wa, jūji han ni demasu.
lines.english: Yes. The local leaves at 10:30.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: じゃあ、急行でお願いします。
lines.english: Then the express, please.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: かしこまりました。
lines.english: Certainly.

contextNotes: Time-telling uses 〜時〜分. Listening focus: じゅうじ じゅうごふん back-to-back is a real beginner trap.
〜も means "also / too." The 急行 (express) vs 普通 (local) distinction is a real traveler decision.
〜に出ます — に marks the time an action happens. Contrast with へ (direction) and で (means): three particles now in play.
〜でお願いします again, reused from 現金で → 急行で. じゃあ = "well then / in that case."

scenarios.japanese: 電車に乗り遅れてしまいました。
scenarios.targetSubstring: 乗り遅れてしまいました

scenario.setting: Back at the desk — the tourist explains a problem and gets reassured.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: すみません、電車に乗り遅れてしまいました。
lines.english: Excuse me, I missed the train.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: あ、それは大変でしたね。大丈夫ですよ。
lines.romaji: A, sore wa taihen deshita ne. Daijōbu desu yo.
lines.english: Oh, that's too bad. It's okay, don't worry.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: このきっぷは、まだ使えますか。
lines.romaji: Kono kippu wa, mada tsukaemasu ka.
lines.english: Can I still use this ticket?

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: はい、次の電車にお乗りいただけます。
lines.romaji: Hai, tsugi no densha ni onori itadakemasu.
lines.english: Yes, you can board the next train.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.japanese: よかった。ありがとうございます。
lines.english: Oh good. Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Attendant
lines.japanese: 次は十一時です。お気をつけて。
lines.romaji: Tsugi wa jūichiji desu. Oki o tsukete.
lines.english: The next one is at 11:00. Take care.

vocabulary: 乗り遅れる / のりおくれる
大丈夫 / だいじょうぶ
お気をつけて / おきをつけて
contextNotes: 〜てしまいました is completion with regret — not just "I missed it" but "I missed it (oops / and I feel bad)." This nuance is the whole reason the form exists.
〜よ gives reassuring new info ("it's fine, trust me"). Contrast with ね.
使える is the potential form of 使う ("can use").
お〜いただけます is polite humble form ("you may kindly ___"). Pure recognition for a beginner — pairs with お待ちください and かしこまりました as service language you can now recognize.
よかった ("thank goodness / what a relief") is a high-frequency, natural emotional reaction.
お気をつけて is a set polite farewell — recognize it, don't dissect it.
